I will keep chili as my main crop because that is what my land and experience are centered on, and it gives me better cash income than maize. My farm is small, only 3.8 mu, and some family labor is away working off-farm, so I will manage it in a way that is steady and not too labor-heavy. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage to protect chili in dry periods and keep maize from stalling after sowing and at key growth stages. I will put most of the land into chili and keep a smaller area in maize for diversification and household needs. For seed, I will use hybrid seed for both crops because I want more uniform growth and better yield stability. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is practical on my small area and faster for me to finish on time. I will use moderate fertilizer rather than pushing too hard, because I want reliable production without excessive cost. Chili needs more water, nutrients, and crop protection, so I will give it more irrigation and more pesticide sprays than maize. Maize is easier for me to manage, so I will keep its inputs lower and use it as the simpler crop in the plan.
